targetText:
That co-operation which is based on division of labour,
assumes its typical form in manufacture, and is the prevalent characteristic
form of the capitalist process of production throughout the manufacturing
period properly so called. That period, roughly speaking, extends from
the middle of the 16th to the last third of the 18th century.
explanation: The manufacturing period (roughly 1550s to 1770s) organized production by splitting crafts into narrow specialized tasks under one roof, foreshadowing the factory system.

targetText:
Formerly the individual work of a Nuremberg
artificer, the watch has been transformed into the social product of an
immense number of detail labourers
explanation: Under manufacture, each worker performs only one tiny fraction of the total production process. This "detail laborer" becomes extremely skilled at their single task but loses the ability to produce a complete product independently.

targetText: If we now go more into detail, it is, in the first place, clear that a labourer who all his life performs one and the same simple operation, converts his whole body into the automatic, specialised implement of that operation.
summary: The detail labourer: lifelong repetitive division of labour turns the worker into an automatic, specialized organ.
explanation: Manufacturing division of labour strips workers of their comprehensive artisanal knowledge, confining each individual to a single repetitive sub-operation. The worker whole body and mind are mutilated to serve as a specialized part of a collective human machine.
context: Part IV, Chapter 14: Division of Labour and Manufacture

targetText: crippled monstrosity, by forcing his detail dexterity at the expense of a world of productive capabilities and instincts; just as in the States of La Plata they butcher a whole beast for the sake of his hide or his tallow.
summary: The crippling of human potential: manufacture suppresses all-round creative capacities to boost detail dexterity.
explanation: Marx passionately critiques how capitalist manufacturing mutilates human faculties. By isolating a single mechanical skill at the expense of general cognitive and physical development, capitalism cripples the worker into an appendage of capital.
context: Part IV, Chapter 14: Division of Labour and Manufacture
